title: Bounded Linear Operators and Quotient Spaces

items.title: A bounded linear operator between normed spaces
For a linear operator, boundedness, continuity at 0, continuity, and Lipschitz continuity are equivalent
items.strategy: A bound \|Tx\|\le C\|x\| gives the global Lipschitz estimate \|Tx-Ty\|\le C\|x-y\|. Conversely, continuity at 0 supplies one small ball mapped into a bounded ball, and linear rescaling turns that local estimate into a global linear bound.

items.title: The operator norm as the least bound and as the unit-sphere or unit-ball supremum
The operator norm is a norm on the space of bounded linear operators
items.strategy: Definiteness uses the unit-sphere supremum, homogeneity is immediate from scalar multiplication, and the triangle inequality comes from \|(S+T)x\|\le\|Sx\|+\|Tx\| before taking suprema.

items.title: Composition satisfies \|ST\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|
items.strategy: Estimate \|STx\| by \|S\|\,\|Tx\| and then by \|S\|\,\|T\|\,\|x\|, followed by the unit-ball supremum.

items.title: The spaces \(\mathcal B(X,Y)\) and \(\mathcal B(X)\) of bounded linear operators
If \(Y\) is Banach then \(\mathcal B(X,Y)\) is Banach
items.strategy: An operator-norm Cauchy sequence is pointwise Cauchy on every vector of X. Completeness of Y gives a pointwise limit T, linearity is inherited pointwise, and the Cauchy bound passes to T to give convergence in operator norm.

items.title: A bounded linear map from a dense normed subspace into a Banach space extends uniquely with the same norm
items.strategy: For each x in the ambient space choose one approximating sequence from the dense subspace. Boundedness makes the image sequence Cauchy in the Banach target, the difference estimate proves independence of the chosen approximants, and linearity and norm preservation follow by passing to the limit. The notes record the selected AC_omega choice of one approximating sequence per point.

items.title: A topological isomorphism of normed spaces
A bounded bilinear map between normed spaces
For a bilinear map, boundedness is equivalent to joint continuity
items.strategy: A product bound controls the three-term expansion of B(x,y)-B(x_0,y_0). Conversely, continuity at (0,0) gives a unit-box estimate for one product norm, and bilinearity rescales that estimate to \|B(x,y)\|\le C\|x\|\,\|y\|.

items.title: The quotient vector space \(X/M\), its cosets, and the quotient map \(q:X\to X/M\)
The quotient seminorm \(\|x+M\|_{X/M}=\inf_{m\in M}\|x+m\|=\operatorname{dist}(x,M)\)
The quotient seminorm is independent of the chosen coset representative
items.strategy: Replacing x by x+m_0 only translates the infimum set by the fixed element m_0, so the set of attainable norms is unchanged.

items.title: The quotient seminorm satisfies the triangle inequality
items.strategy: Choose epsilon-minimizers m_1 and m_2 for the two cosets and estimate \|x+y+(m_1+m_2)\| by the ambient triangle inequality before letting epsilon go to zero.

items.title: The quotient seminorm is a norm exactly when the subspace is closed
items.strategy: The null classes are exactly the cosets x+M with dist(x,M)=0, hence the image of the closure of M in X/M. So the seminorm is definite exactly when that null space is M itself.

items.title: The quotient map sends every open ball onto a set containing the corresponding quotient ball
items.strategy: If \|x+M\|<r, choose an epsilon-minimizer m with \|x+m\|<r and note that q(x+m)=q(x). Translation then reduces arbitrary open balls to the ball about zero.

items.title: A quotient of a Banach space by a closed subspace is Banach
items.strategy: Start from a rapidly Cauchy subsequence in the quotient, choose lifts of successive increments with norms below 2^{-k}+2^{-2k}, sum those lifts in X by the Banach series criterion, and then recover a limit for the original quotient sequence.

items.title: A bounded operator that vanishes on a subspace factors uniquely through the normed quotient
items.strategy: Use the published algebraic quotient universal property to define the factor on cosets, prove representative independence before any norm estimate, bound the factor by taking the infimum over representatives, and use the quotient-ball theorem to recover equality of operator norms.

items.title: A complemented closed subspace of a normed space
A closed subspace is complemented exactly when it is the range of a bounded projection
items.strategy: If X=M\oplus N with bounded coordinate projections, the projection onto M is idempotent and has range M. Conversely, an idempotent P gives the direct-sum splitting X=ran(P)\oplus ker(P) with coordinate projections P and I-P.

items.title: A bounded operator that is bounded below
For a bounded operator between Banach spaces, being bounded below is equivalent to being injective with closed range
items.strategy: A lower bound makes injectivity immediate and turns every convergent image sequence into a Cauchy preimage sequence, so the range is closed. Conversely, once the range is closed it is Banach, so T:X\to ran(T) is a bounded bijection between Banach spaces; re-run the inverse-operator proof on that range using the published complete-metric Baire theorem to obtain a bound on T^{-1}, hence a lower bound on T.

items.title: Bounded left inverses and bounded right inverses
A surjective bounded operator between Banach spaces has a bounded right inverse exactly when its kernel is complemented
items.strategy: If S is a right inverse then x=(x-STx)+STx splits X into ker(T) and ran(S). Conversely, if ker(T) has a closed complement L, then T|_L is a bounded bijection from the Banach space L onto Y; item 23 gives a lower bound on T|_L, so its inverse is bounded and yields the desired right inverse.

items.title: An injective bounded operator between Banach spaces has a bounded left inverse exactly when its range is closed and complemented
items.strategy: If S is a left inverse then T(X) is closed because T(x_n) convergent implies x_n=S(Tx_n) convergent, and Y=T(X)\oplus ker(S). Conversely, if T(X) is closed and complemented, project Y onto T(X) and compose that projection with the bounded inverse of T:X\to T(X) supplied by item 23.
